rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Refuting Simulation Theory and New Age Gnosticism", "body": "Chance described refuting simulation theory as one of his bigger life missions, calling it the materialist version of an old prison-world philosophy that keeps resurfacing. He argued that many conspiracy researchers followed breadcrumbs to the conclusion that the world is illusion, and he blamed lazy research built on secondhand interpretation of texts. The hosts asked him to define his terms, and Chance described transhumanists, programmers, and spiritual seekers who read growing synchronicities as proof of a fake world. He credited Neville Goddard for the view that consciousness comes first and expression follows."}, {"title": "Constellation Writing and the Flood Story", "body": "Chance described the Sumerian and Akkadian term Lumashi as constellation writing, and said priest astronomers recorded history in the sky. He offered it as his opinion that conquerors had hostage priests place kings and events among the stars, so the sky became a record. Chance compared Noah with the Sumerian flood hero Atrahasis, then pointed to Orion, the Argo Navis, a dove star, and a raven constellation as the flood story's components. He recommended a planisphere and John McHugh's book The Celestial Code of Scripture."}, {"title": "Etymology, Letter Swaps, and Nag Hammadi", "body": "Chance used the name Nag Hammadi to demonstrate his language keys. He read Nag as serpent, Ham as dark, and Mad as mother or maker, and he said letters such as L and R, or D and K, interchange between languages. He applied the same method to Sophia, Pistis, Adonai, and Archon. A host noted that Pistis means belief in modern Greek, and Chance agreed it connected to epistemology. He also said the most popular translation of the texts was prepared by UNESCO, calling that problematic, and stressed he made no claim that the doctrine was accurate."}, {"title": "Victim Posture, Plant Medicine, and the Body", "body": "Chance said that believing the world is a prison hands a person the ultimate victim posture, and that escape practices can turn selfish. When the hosts raised plant medicine, he called it a tool that is neither good nor bad, and described psilocybin and Qi Gong as helpful in his own path. A host described sobriety and somatic bodywork as his biggest changes. Chance also said he believed the archons are human, and he separated subjective experience from consensus reality. He described biofield tuning as a language for communicating with the body."}, {"title": "The Trinity, the Destroyer, and the Demiurge", "body": "Chance described emanations and the trinity as an ancient doctrine of creator, destroyer, and regenerator, which he linked to the sun's seasons and to the vesica piscis. He offered his opinion that the devil idea arose when people split the destroyer from the regenerator and treated it as a separate being. He read a passage about Eve from the Origin of the World text and traced the name Maya through several mythologies. Yerasimos remarked that the three people on the call formed a trinity, and Chance answered a Tao Te Ching line about three with a statement attributed to Hermes, which he linked to the sun's figure eight path."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I joined Joel Rafidi and Yerasimos on Episode 97 of the Here For The Truth podcast to talk through my research on simulation theory and New Age Gnosticism. We looked at the Nag Hammadi texts, the Demiurge and the Archons, and the language and astrotheology behind them.
